question:
Patient note:
A 90-year-old man who lives alone in a single-story cottage and still drives himself to the grocery store was referred to the peri-operative medicine clinic this morning by ophthalmology for fitness assessment before a scheduled left cataract extraction under monitored anesthesia care. He walked from the waiting area with a steady, slightly stooped gait while leaning on an adjustable cane that he primarily carries for knee discomfort rather than balance, and he conversed easily with staff, recalling the exact dates of three grandchildren’s birthdays and the current value of his pension fund, indicating preserved short-term memory and executive function. Six years ago he was admitted for an acute right-sided facial droop and expressive aphasia that were confirmed on cranial imaging as an infarct in the left middle cerebral artery territory; alteplase was administered within two hours, and after a ten-day inpatient rehabilitation course he recovered fluent speech and full limb strength, with only a mildly slowed finger-to-nose test on the right that does not interfere with daily activities such as buttoning shirts or typing e-mails. He has not experienced further focal events, and a surveillance carotid duplex performed last winter showed less than 30 % luminal narrowing bilaterally. Pulmonary history is notable for chronic airflow obstruction traced to a 65-pack-year cigarette habit that he discontinued a decade ago when his first great-grandchild was born. Since then he has used a once-daily long-acting muscarinic antagonist inhaler and a budesonide–formoterol combination twice daily; he keeps albuterol in his jacket for exertional wheeze when climbing the slight incline to his mailbox but empties only one 200-dose canister every three months. He reports two winter flares in the past five years requiring five-day courses of prednisone but has never needed ventilatory support or been hospitalized overnight for respiratory issues. Baseline spirometry obtained two months ago recorded an FEV₁ of 1.3 L (55 % predicted) with an FEV₁/FVC ratio of 0.55 and less than 8 % post-bronchodilator change; resting pulse oximetry in clinic today is 95 % on ambient air with a respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute. Cardiac review is reassuring: he denies substernal pressure, exertional diaphoresis, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, leg swelling, or recent weight gain, and a transthoracic echocardiogram performed last year for murmur evaluation revealed an ejection fraction of 60 %, normal chamber dimensions, and only trace aortic sclerosis. He walks his small terrier three blocks twice daily, stopping once to catch his breath on chilly mornings because of wheeze rather than fatigue, and he sleeps on a single pillow. Past laboratory workup by hepatology uncovered mildly elevated transaminases (aspartate aminotransferase 41 U/L, alanine aminotransferase 44 U/L) with normal bilirubin and albumin; ultrasound demonstrated homogeneous increased echogenicity without nodularity, and the team attributed the findings to remote non-cirrhotic hepatitis C that achieved sustained virologic response after a three-month direct-acting antiviral course eight years ago. He has never developed jaundice, abdominal distention, easy bruising, encephalopathy, or gastrointestinal bleeding, and coagulation indices remain stable (international normalized ratio 1.1 last week). Metabolic screening yesterday showed fasting plasma glucose 98 mg/dL and glycated hemoglobin 5.6 %, values he maintains through portion control rather than medication; he denies polyuria, polydipsia, neuropathic tingling, or retina complaints, and dilated fundus examination six months ago was unremarkable except for the cataract now slated for extraction. Renal function is preserved with serum creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, blood urea nitrogen 18 mg/dL, estimated glomerular filtration rate 70 mL/min/1.73 m², sodium 138 mmol/L, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, chloride 103 mmol/L, and bicarbonate 24 mmol/L; urinalysis is bland without protein, blood, or casts. He denies epigastric pain, dyspepsia, hematemesis, or tarry stools and has never required acid suppression beyond occasional calcium carbonate after spicy meals. There is no personal or family history of hematologic malignancy, systemic inflammatory disorders, or immunocompromise. Current medications include tiotropium 18 µg each dawn, budesonide–formoterol 160/4.5 µg two puffs twice daily, albuterol 90 µg as needed, low-dose aspirin 81 mg daily initiated after the stroke, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, vitamin D3 1000 IU daily, and acetaminophen 500 mg for knee aches; he reports an itchy rash to sulfonamide antibiotics in his thirties but no other drug allergies. He drinks one glass of red wine with Sunday dinner, never used illicit substances, and has not returned to smoking. Review of systems is negative for fever, chills, night sweats, unintended weight loss, productive cough, hemoptysis, dizziness, syncope, visual loss beyond the cataract, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, hematochezia, dysuria, or rash. On examination he is thin, sits comfortably, and speaks in full sentences without accessory-muscle use. Vital signs: temperature 36.7 °C, blood pressure 126/64 mm Hg seated in the left arm, heart rate 72 beats/min regular, respiratory rate as noted, and body-mass index 23 kg/m². Conjunctivae are pink, sclerae anicteric. Neck is supple with brisk carotid upstrokes and no bruit; jugular venous pulsation measures 3 cm above the sternal angle at 45°. The point of maximal impulse is palpable in the fifth intercostal space mid-clavicular line without displacement; S1 and S2 are crisp, with an early peaking systolic ejection sound over the right second interspace but no gallops or rubs. Percussion of the chest is mildly hyperresonant; breath sounds are diminished at the bases with occasional scattered expiratory wheezes but no crackles. Abdomen is flat, soft, nontender, with a liver edge palpable 1 cm below the costal margin, smooth and non-tender; there is no splenomegaly or ascites, and bowel sounds are normoactive. Extremities are warm with 2+ radial, dorsalis pedis, and posterior tibial pulses, capillary refill under two seconds, and no edema or digital clubbing. Neurologic testing shows alert affect, orientation to person, place, time, and situation, cranial nerves II–XII intact, 5/5 strength throughout, symmetric reflexes, normal vibration and proprioception to the toes, and a slightly wide-based but steady tandem gait; rapid alternating movements are mildly slowed on the right hand. A 12-lead electrocardiogram recorded in clinic demonstrates normal sinus rhythm at 70 beats/min, PR interval 160 ms, QRS duration 94 ms, axis 10°, and no pathologic Q waves or ST-segment shifts. A posteroanterior chest radiograph from this morning shows hyperinflated lungs with flattened diaphragms, vascular markings unchanged from prior studies, and a normal cardiac silhouette. The ophthalmic team seeks recommendations on peri-operative inhaler scheduling, continuation of antiplatelet therapy around the time of lens extraction, and guidance on fluid management in view of his age and preserved yet borderline renal reserve.

Question: What is the patient's Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index adds age points to weighted baseline comorbidities.
- Age: 50–59, 60–69, 70–79, and ≥80 years score 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively. At 90, he scores 4.
- Cerebrovascular disease: prior ischemic stroke = 1. Strength is 5/5; mild incoordination is not hemiplegia.
- Chronic pulmonary disease: COPD with persistent airflow obstruction = 1.
- Mild liver disease: noncirrhotic hepatitis history with persistent mild transaminase elevation = 1. No portal hypertension or hepatic decompensation supports a higher weight.
- Other qualifying comorbidities = 0. In particular, there is no documented heart failure, diabetes, moderate-to-severe renal disease, or malignancy.
Total: 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 7.
Final answer: 7
